context.content: **Background:** I've been using Evernote for a few years. Have about 1,000 notes in Evernote. Use it primarily for typing notes and scanning in handwritten notes (which I then summarize in typed text above or below the typed pages). I also occasionally save web clippings, PDFs, and other media into Evernote for things related to my work (mostly reports, news articles, etc). I saved a fair amount of personal stuff in Evernote, including family information (like contracts for home improvement stuff, records of customer service calls, notes re: pediatrician visits, etc) and other personal stuff (receipts, records of purchases, some medical info, etc). Evernote was used mostly for note taking and also for keeping track of things, a bit like a filing cabinet. I DID NOT tend to annotate PDFs. My most-used feature was taking notes for work and scanning in handwritten notes and documents I'd annotated by hand. My reliance on Evernote increased this year when my workplace went mostly-remote. Without a full-time physical office, I needed to reduce the amount of shit I carry around. I work about 50% of the time on a PC for work, but always have an iPhone and iPad with me (and iPad use has drastically increased compared to my PC use in the last month). More and more my notes were being taken on my iPad so that I could avoid carrying around piles of paper. During personal time, most everything is done on my iPhone or iPad. **Evernote Frustrations:** Like many people, I developed a number of concerns / frustrations re: Evernote. I wasn't terribly upset when they changed their pricing structure but was more frustrated with the bad, glitchy UI. The loss of dark mode was HUGELY frustrating for me. I do a lot of work in low-light and the bright white screen was painful to look at for a long period of time. I also saw an increase in syncing issues and was experiencing more and more frustrations when trying to just take basic notes (i.e., in a meeting or at a conference). Outlines and bulleted lists were so frustrating to quickly create, the app was horrid to look at, the annoying copy/paste bug was still there, notebooks and tags all started to seem redundant and clunky, and the whole UI began to feel really cluttered in general. As I increased my reliance on the app for taking notes, my frustrations with it grew. **Options Considered:** I tried One Note and didn't care for it. Apple Notes doesn't have enough options for organization and doesn't make it easy to export notes. A few other apps didn't seem well supported or were only available on iPad. Ulysses became wicked expensive recently. I wanted something that supported markdown and was nimble, fast, and pleasant to look at. Cost wasn't a huge factor, but I wanted to make sure I was was getting good value for my money. When I downloaded Bear I was immediately drawn to its UI and tagging system. Right away I could tell it was nimble, fast, and intuitive. **The Transition:** I used my Mac to export all my Evernote notes and move them into Bear. It took just a few minutes. Things were a little messy at first, but bulk editing tags in Bear is wicked easy. I only had to go into about 1/8 of my notes and remove extraneous tags. I also took the time to delete a lot of notes that were no longer needed. I re-tagged a lot of my imported notes and streamlined my tagging system (had WAY too many tags in Evernote, most of which made no sense). Within 24 hours of just periodically going in and cleaning things up and putting a little thought into my new system (did a lot of it while out walking the dog and waiting in line at the grocery store), all my old notes were organized in a much more efficient tagging system. Definitely take the time to read Bear's "welcome" notes. They are incredibly helpful. Don't worry if you want to change how a group of notes is tagged. It's REALLY easy! I don't miss my notebooks and stacks at all (and that was something I was really concerned about). **Bear, what I like:** * The UI is beautiful. It's a pleasure to look at and use, and the themes make it so that you have a view that works in pretty much any setting. * It's nimble and fast, especially for taking notes. Seriously, if your primary function is note taking, this app excels where Evernote and One Note both fail. * Syncing works perfectly. * You can export your note in a variety of formats. Sometimes I'll type something up in Bear and then export it in a Word doc (.docx) format for work stuff. Having a variety of export options makes this a very functional drafting app. I do a lot of writing for work and hate working in Word. Now, all my stuff starts in Bear and only ends up in Word when it's being finalized. * Search function is fast. It works very well. * It's an ideal environment for drafting on the iPhone. This is important because many of my notes and ideas begin on my iPhone, and then I move on to my iPad or Mac. * Extensions work well. I've saved a number of articles from Safari and other apps via the extension feature. I'm also playing around with Workflows (for example, I used Workflow to create a widget to quickly create a new note). * The company seems to have a vision. Evernote clearly lost their vision at some point and that ultimately hurt their product. Even though Bear is young, it is pretty bug-free and very polished. The vision as a note taking and writing app is clear. For writing, I actually like it better than Ulysses. For note taking, it's superior to pretty much everything out there in terms of UI and functionality. **Bear, Limitations/things to consider:** * To move from Evernote to Bear, you really need access to a Mac. You can export from Evernote via a PC, but I'm not sure how you'd then get the notes into Bear (maybe Dropbox?) * Bear only works on iOS / Mac. This is the biggest drawback. It really needs some web or PC support, but I realize this might limit the use of iCloud sync. The sync works beautifully now so I would hate to see that lost. I recently purchased an iPad so I'm using that for note taking in the office environment. But if you don't have this option, don't want to be locked into iOS / OS, and /or only have access to a PC or Android device for part of your day, Bear might not work. I'm making it work, but some sort of cross-platform support would be helpful. * No OCR support. My work around for this is to use Scanbot, and then export both the PDF and plaintext into a BearNote via the extension. This makes the document functionally searchable. I don't do this a ton but it works for when I need to do it. * You cannot do tables. I didn't use them much in Evernote but this feature in Bear would be helpful. * No colored text. I miss this a little and hope Bear adds ability to at least change the color of the highlighter. When typing work notes, I sometimes need to make certain text stand out. * There are a lot of other little things in Evernote. Most of those features (like scanning business cards and importing contact info) weren't things I used anyway. But consider whether loss of those types of features will hurt your workflow. To me, it was mostly just bloat. * Bear takes up more storage space compared to Evernote. On my iPhone, Bear takes up just under 1GB, whereas Evernote takes up just 102 MB. In iCloud, Bear takes up a considerable amount of storage space (636 MB). Make sure you have enough room both on your device and in iCloud. **User suggestions for Bear Devs** * Web app (or some other cross-platform support) * Auto-completion of tags within a note. Sometimes I can't remember exactly how I tagged something before. This would be helpful if possible. * OCR support * Ability to change highlighter color * Custom themes * More security options (e.g., encryption, locking notes/app, basically any improvements in the area of privacy and security would be appreciated). **Tl;dr:** Bear is an excellent replacement for Evernote, with a much cleaner UI and better functionality for note taking. Moving from Evernote to Bear wasn't as hard as I anticipated. Bear's tagging system is much better than folders and stacks. Most significant feature loss is the cross-platform and in-app OCR support. If you can make it work in iOS/OS only, get Bear. It's better. The little Bear makes me smile every time I open the app.
